title: Regionalt odontoligiskt ansvarig - Smile Södra Norrland
description:
Var med och skapa Sveriges bästa tandvård tillsammans med oss! 💙

Här får du gehör för dina tankar och idéer – i teamet, på kliniken och i hela Smile. Vi erbjuder en hälsosam och trygg arbetsmiljö där varje medarbetare får möjligheten att växa. Vi sätter kvaliteten och patientens behov i fokus genom utbildning och personlig utveckling. Med vår prestigelösa ledarstil och starka teamanda kommer du att känna dig hörd, uppskattad och delaktig. Hos Smile skapar vi en hållbar framtid där varje medarbetare bidrar till vår gemensamma framgång - Vi vet att vi är bäst tillsammans!

Nu söker vi en regionalt odontologiskt ansvarig till Södra Norrland. Ta chansen att bli en del av Smile och bidra till framtidens tandvård!

Vilka är Smile?

🌎 Sveriges största privata tandvårdskedja - det är viktigt för oss att finnas tillgängliga för våra patienter i hela landet - inte begränsa oss till varken små- eller storstad.

👨‍⚕️ Över 65 kliniker och 1100 medarbetare. Här får du bli en del av ett stort nätverk och vår bredd ger stora möjligheter för både utbildning och personlig utveckling.

💙 Collaboration,Care & Entrepreneurship - vår värdegrund.

😃 Vår vision - friska leenden i hela Sverige! Här siktar Smile på att verka för friska patienter i hela landet och skapa varma leenden hos våra medarbetare genom vår unika kultur.

🙌 Tillsammans med våra systerorganisationer inom Colosseum Dental Group erbjuder vi tandvård för fler än 3 miljoner patienter i 11 länder i Europa.

Att vara ROA hos Smile Tandvård

I rollen som ROA ansvarar du för klinisk verksamhetsutveckling på klinikerna i din region. Detta arbete koordinerar och arbetsleder du tillsammans med Odontologisk ansvariga (OA) och Platschefer ute på dina kliniker. Du ingår i regionledningen och i rollen som ROA rapporterar du till Regionchef. Som ROA arbetar du tätt tillsammans med regionledning, Nationellt Odontologisk Ansvarig (NOA) och OA (se bild nedan på rollfördelning mellan NOA, ROA och Kvalitetsansvarig).

Utöver detta innefattar dina arbetsuppgifter . att du:

  • Prioriterar och driver projekt på regionnivå

  • Stöttar i klinisk verksamhetsutveckling och uppföljning av de projekt som drivs i regionen tillsammans med regionledning, NOA och lokala OA

  • Stöttar Regionchefen i rekryteringen av nya OA

  • Driver utbildningsagenda på regionnivå

  • Täcker upp som klinik-OA vid vakans

  • Stöttar Kvalitetsansvarig vid t.ex. vissa kundklagomålsärenden


Vem söker vi?

Smile Tandvårds medarbetare är avgörande för vår framgång. Därför är din inställning och personlighet A & O för oss. I den här rollen ser vi att det är viktigt att du har ett starkt intresse för att driva och utveckla odontologin i regionen på ett strukturerat sätt. Du tycker om att driva projekt och frågor självständigt och är inte rädd för att ta tag i problem eller svårare frågeställningar. Vidare är du kommunikativ, social och har ett intresse för affären.

Utöver ovan kompetenser ser vi att du har:

  • Tandläkar- eller specialistlegitimation

  • Goda språkkunskaper i svenska och engelska i tal och skrift

  • Tidigare erfarenhet som OA


Anställningsform och tillträde

Rollen omfattar motsvarande 20% tjänstgöring och kombineras med klinisk tjänstgöring på klinik och eventuellt lokalt OA-ansvar för din hemmaklinik. ROA kan också komma att ta lokalt OA ansvar för mindre kliniker (1-3 behandlare) i regionen.


Ansökan och frågor

Vill du också vara med och bidra till att skapa Sveriges bästa tandvård? Då tror vi att den här tjänsten kan vara något för dig! Du skickar in din ansökan genom vårt ansökningsformulär, så återkommer vi till dig via mail eller telefon för återkoppling så snart vi har möjlighet. Sista ansökningsdag är 3 december. Vi arbetar löpande med vårt urval, vilket innebär att tjänsten kan komma att tillsättas innan sista ansökningsdag.

Vi tror på forskningsbaserade och objektiva utvärderingsmetoder som stöd i arbetet att hitta rätt person till rätt roll. Därför använder vi oss utav arbetspsykologiska tester, kompetensbaserade intervjuer och bakgrundskontroll i våra rekryteringsprocesser. Här på vår karriärsida kan du läsa mer om stegen i vår kompetensbaserade rekryteringsprocess. I rekryteringsprocessen genomför vi bakgrundskontroll via Verifiera, IVO & Hosp i samband med referenstagning.

Vid frågor kontakta Regionchef Pernilla Oskarsson pernilla.oskarsson@smile.se, eller ansvarig rekryterare Ebba Härnstam ebba.harnstam@smile.se .

Smiles erbjudande

🦷 Odontologi - kärnan i allt vi gör! Här erbjuder vi dig en arbetsplats med odontologi och kvalité som kärna i vår kultur med stark gemenskap.

👩‍⚕️ Vill du ta del av medarbetarberättelser och lära känna några av våra stjärnor? Läs mer HÄR.

🚀 En av Sveriges bästa arbetsplatser 2025 & 2026 enligt Great Place to Work! Läs pressmeddelandet HÄR.

🏆 Vi vill vara branschens bästa arbetsgivare. Därför är vi extra stolta över att ha fått ta emot utmärkelserna Årets Karriärföretag 2024, 2025 & 2026 samt Great Place to Work. HÄR kan du läsa mer om dessa utmärkelser.

💡 Vi älskar kompetensutveckling! Hos oss är utveckling A & O. Därför är vi stolta över de utbildnings- och utvecklingsmöjligheter vi erbjuder våra medarbetare. Läs mer HÄR.

🎉 Vi firar framgångar! Och vi har självklart goda villkor och förmåner för att du är viktig för oss. Läs mer om vårt erbjudande till dig HÄR.

title: Growth & Conversion Manager
description:
Every renter who lands on our site is looking for a home, and every visit that ends without a conversation is someone we didn't get to help. Smart City is looking for a Growth & Conversion Manager who is curious about why people do what they do on a website, and has the data skills to prove it. You will own the numbers that tell us what is working, from tagging and GA4 to attribution. Then you will use them to run an ongoing program of tests that turns more visitors into leads across our landing pages, listing pages, and forms. When we open a new city, you will lead the marketing launch, so each market goes live with pages that convert, tracking that works from day one, and spend paced to the agents ready to serve it. This is a hands-on role with no direct reports, reporting to the Senior Director of Performance & Growth, Marketing and working closely with paid media, our web developer and agency, Technology, and our local market teams.

What You'll Do

  • Own marketing measurement: tagging, Google Tag Manager, GA4, conversion tracking, and attribution, so every channel reports leads and leases the same way
  • Build and maintain the foundations: one lead definition across Google Ads, Meta, GA4, and our CRM, offline conversion feedback to the ad platforms, and clean, documented tracking
  • Run a testing program across landing pages, listing and deal pages, and forms, from hypothesis to result to rollout
  • Own landing page optimization for paid campaigns, working with paid media and the creative team on pages built for each channel and market
  • Study the full path from first visit to submitted lead, using analytics, session recordings, and renter feedback to find where people drop off and why
  • Set the conversion roadmap with the Senior Director, and work with our web developer / agency to ship changes within an agreed share of their time
  • Lead marketing for new market launches: the launch plan, market pages, tracking, paid setup, and spend paced to local agent capacity. Partner with Market Expansion, local market managers, and our agency to make each one happen
  • Report conversion rates, test results, and launch performance to the Senior Director, with clear recommendations
  • Keep tracking and consent compliant with privacy rules, and keep pages and tests within Fair Housing guidelines

Who We're Looking For

  • 7 to 10 years of experience in growth, conversion rate optimization, or marketing analytics, with a record of measurable conversion gains
  • Deep, hands-on expertise in GA4 and Google Tag Manager, including conversion tracking for Google Ads and Meta (Conversions API, Enhanced Conversions)
  • Experience building attribution and connecting ad platforms to a CRM, including offline conversion imports
  • A track record running an A/B testing program, with sound judgment on sample size, significance, and when to call a test
  • Enough HTML, CSS, and JavaScript to build tests and debug tracking, plus experience with testing tools such as VWO, Optimizely, or similar
  • Strong analytical skills: SQL or BI tools (Looker Studio, Tableau, or similar), and funnel and cohort analysis
  • Experience managing launches or complex projects with many stakeholders and fixed dates
  • A clear communicator who turns data into recommendations people act on
  • Bachelor's degree required, ideally in marketing, business, economics, statistics, or a related field
  • Self-directed, organized, and comfortable with ambiguity in a people-first culture

Nice to Have

  • Experience launching marketing in new cities for a multi-location business
  • Experience in real estate, rentals, proptech, or a two-sided marketplace
  • WordPress experience
  • Privacy and consent tools (Cookiebot, Google Consent Mode)
  • Session analytics tools such as Hotjar or Microsoft Clarity

Physical Requirements

  • Travel to and touring properties around the city may periodically be required.
  • Travel to other markets may periodically be required.
  • Assures that safety regulations are followed at all times.
  • Adherence to compliance measures implemented by governing bodies such as but not limited to OSHA & the CDC. Follows policies and procedures including infection control, universal precautions, and exposure control plans when performing daily tasks.
  • Reports hazardous conditions, accidents, and incidents to the immediate supervisor.
  • Must be able to lift up to 25 lbs.
  • Requires standing, walking, bending, kneeling, stooping and crouching.

Expected Hours of Work

  • Typical business hours: 8:30am - 5:30pm Monday - Friday, availability for escalations may be needed outside of normal business hours.

Travel

  • Up to 10% of the time.
  • Minimal travel may be required for business functions, team training, and culture events.

Compensation & Benefits

  • Eligibility for medical, dental, and vision coverage as well as a 401(k) plan subject to plan terms.
  • Eligibility for company-paid benefits such as company-paid and voluntary life insurance, short & long-term disability, and parental leave subject to applicable waiting periods.

description:
Smart City is looking for Content Capture Specialists to capture the photos and video that help renters choose their next apartment. You will travel to apartment communities in cities across the country, capturing professional property photography, social-first short-form video, and drone footage, then editing, checking, and delivering a complete asset library for each property. Your work serves Smart City Digital's multifamily clients and covers most of the photo and video Smart City Locating uses across its markets and channels. You own the finished asset library; our Content Creation team turns it into monthly client content. We are hiring two remote specialists, one based in the West (ideally Phoenix or Denver) and one in the East (ideally Charlotte, Orlando, or Atlanta), and the role travels 90% to 100% of the time. This is a hands-on role with no direct reports, reporting to the Managing Director of Smart City Digital and working closely with our Client Success & Operations Specialist, who handles scheduling, travel, and property access, and our Content Creation Specialists.

What You'll Do

  • Capture assigned properties for Smart City Digital clients and Smart City Locating: professional real estate photography, social-first short-form and UGC-style video, drone photo and video, and neighborhood and lifestyle content
  • Hit weekly capture targets for quality, completeness, volume, and turnaround, with targets rising as you ramp up
  • Follow shot lists, capture briefs, client requirements, and brand guidelines so every property ends up with a complete, usable library
  • Edit photography with our approved workflows and presets so color, composition, and presentation stay consistent across properties
  • Upload, label, and organize final assets in our asset system so Content Creation Specialists can find the right content fast
  • Quality-check every library before handoff, and catch missing shots, technical problems, or reshoot needs before a property is marked complete
  • Fly drones safely, within applicable regulations, certifications, and Smart City Digital standards
  • Represent Smart City Digital on-site: confirm access and readiness when you arrive, work smoothly with property teams, follow each property's dos and don'ts, and flag model-unit, amenity, weather, or construction issues early
  • Spot what makes each property and neighborhood stand out, and capture it along with authentic social-first moments
  • Keep cameras, lenses, drones, batteries, and storage ready, and keep your manager and the Client Success & Operations Specialist current on shoot, upload, and editing status
  • Share field feedback that improves scheduling, shot lists, capture SOPs, presets, and training, and cross-train with the other specialists so any of you can cover any property
  • Cover for teammates during PTO, busy periods, reshoots, and refresh captures


Who We're Looking For

  • Ideally 2+ years of professional photography, videography, content production, or social content capture experience
  • Experience shooting real estate, architectural, interior, hospitality, or lifestyle photography
  • Experience filming short-form, UGC, or social-first video
  • Strong photo editing in Adobe Lightroom and Photoshop or comparable tools, with repeatable workflows and presets
  • Strong photography fundamentals: composition, exposure, lighting, perspective, and framing
  • Working knowledge of professional cameras, lenses, drones, and storage media. Drone experience is preferred, and you must be able to obtain and maintain any required commercial drone certification to fly on your own
  • Comfortable traveling 90% to 100% of the time, including overnight and multi-day trips, and adapting to weather, access issues, and shifting schedules
  • A valid driver's license
  • Organized and detail-oriented: you follow shot lists, naming conventions, and SOPs, and you keep large asset libraries clean
  • Self-managed in the field: you balance travel, shoots, uploads, editing, and deadlines, and you raise problems early
  • A professional, friendly presence with property teams and clients, and open to feedback and coaching
  • High school diploma or equivalent required; an associate's or bachelor's degree in photography, film, media, marketing, communications, or a related field is a plus

Nice to Have

  • Experience with travel-based field production or high-volume, multi-location shoots
  • Video editing in CapCut, Splice, Adobe Premiere, or similar
  • Experience flying DJI drones
  • Experience organizing and delivering large digital asset libraries
  • Project management tools such as ClickUp, Asana, or Monday.com, plus Google Workspace, macOS, and iOS

Physical Requirements

  • Assures that safety regulations are followed at all times.
  • Adherence to compliance measures implemented by governing bodies such as but not limited to OSHA & the CDC. Follows policies and procedures including infection control, universal precautions, and exposure control plans when performing daily tasks.
  • Reports hazardous conditions, accidents, and incidents to the immediate supervisor.
  • Must be able to lift up to 25 lbs.
  • Requires standing, walking, bending, kneeling, stooping and crouching.

Expected Hours of Work

  • Schedules flex around capture needs. Work generally happens during normal business hours, but shoots may require early mornings, golden-hour or evening capture, resident and neighborhood events, and weekend availability.

Travel

  • 90% to 100% of the time, including overnight and multi-day trips, based on client capture volume, market demand, and team coverage needs.
  • Occasional travel for team training, business meetings, and company culture events.

Compensation & Benefits

  • Salary range for this role is $47,500 to $54,000
  • Eligibility for medical, dental, and vision coverage as well as a 401(k) plan subject to plan terms.
  • Eligibility for company-paid benefits such as company-paid and voluntary life insurance, short & long-term disability, and parental leave subject to applicable waiting periods.
  • Flexible PTO
  • Company-Recognized Paid Holidays
  • Monthly cell phone stipend

Stratolaunch is seeking a hands-on Crew Chief (CC) to lead the aircraft maintenance team in the efficient execution of the work scope performed to the aircraft; maintenance, preventive maintenance, inspections, and alterations. This role demands a highly skilled individual with attention to detail and a commitment to upholding the standards set by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) for airworthiness and safety. The candidate should thrive in a high paced environment and be comfortable with the design, development, and test life cycle of rapid aerospace R&D. This role will include daily interactions with engineers and managers, so strong communication and interpersonal skills are required. This position will work directly with the Director of Maintenance, Maintenance Manager, Engineering, Management, and Aircraft Maintenance Team.

ESSENTIAL RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Ensure the aircraft is maintained in an airworthy condition in accordance with the inspection plan and adhering to established standards such as AC 43-13, technical manuals, blueprints, or sketches for acceptable systems installation methods, techniques, and practices
  • Take ownership of the aircraft and all quality of work performed
  • Responsible for ALL aspects of mission launch and recovery ground operations
  • Responsible for coordinating with engineering disciplines to draft the maintenance documentation and checklists for the aircraft that will be used during testing and will be submitted to the FAA as part of the airworthiness documentation package
  • Hands-on working CC providing leadership and mentorship to aircraft maintenance team. Set clear expectations for performance and accountability. Develop talent through training, coaching, and feedback.
  • Mentor and train Assistant Crew Chief (A/CC) in CC duties and responsibilities in order to maintain program continuity in the event the CC is unavailable.
  • Oversee day to day management of all areas of ground operations, direct activities and ensure that schedules, policies, and procedures are met while staying within quality standards and cost objectives
  • Carry out supervisory responsibilities in accordance with the organization's policies and applicable laws. Responsibilities include training employees, planning, assigning, and directing work, appraising performance, addressing complaints, and resolving problems
  • Conduct on-the-job training (OJT) on systems and maintenance procedures such as, pre-flight, post flight inspections, flight controls, landing gear, electrical, avionics, and propulsion systems
  • Schedule daily crew meetings to include, but not limited to, relaying pertinent information, work scope, training, safety, and other sensitive and relevant company information to aid the aircraft maintenance team in proper performance of their duties
  • Responsible for overall safety of the team and aircraft during all ground operations
  • Ensure proper and timely entry of maintenance performed in the Aircraft Maintenance Discrepancy Log (MDL) and Electronic Maintenance database (Jira)
  • Complete logbook records in accordance with Company policy and FAA regulations
  • Sign-off required aircraft forms to Return aircraft to Service
  • Support any FAA activities as required
  • Assist in implementing FOD Control and Tool Control processes
  • Able to communicate at all levels of the organization and with customers as required
  • Communicate vehicle status on all aspects to Director of Ground Operations, Flight OPS, Engineering, and Aircraft Maintenance Team
  • Responsible for team welfare, morale and for providing a fun, yet professional working environment
  • Demonstrate honesty, responsibility, integrity, and fulfillment of commitments

QUALIFICATIONS

  • Possess a working knowledge of the Federal Aviation Regulations and airworthiness requirements.
  • Possess a working knowledge of aircraft factory modifications, service bulletins, inspection program requirements, vendor information and all other procedures, publications and general information pertaining to aircraft
  • Knowledge of all systems e.g. electrical, pneumatic, hydraulics, landing gear, engines.
  • Proven leadership, organizational and interpersonal skills
  • Strong problem solving and analytical skills
  • Must have strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Have a working knowledge of Jira preferred
  • Proficient knowledge of MS Office (Word, Excel, and PowerPoint)
  • Ability to obtain and maintain a DoD Secret security clearance
  • Must be willing to work a flexible work schedule

EDUCATION & EXPERIENCE

  • 3-5 years experience in leadership and management of flight-line & maintenance operations (preferred)
  • 7+ years of experience in aircraft systems fabrication, installation, and maintenance (preferred)

Special remarks regarding work environment, if applicable

title: Senior IT Coordinator
description:
The Asia Group (TAG) is now accepting applications for a Senior IT Coordinator to join our team based in Gurugram.

Headquartered in Washington, D.C., The Asia Group (“TAG”) is a strategic and capital advisory firm that positions clients – ranging from Fortune 100 multinationals to innovative startups – for success in established and emerging markets across the Indo-Pacific region. Our diverse team possesses decades of government and private sector experience with a work ethos that emphasizes teamwork, collegiality, creativity, entrepreneurialism, and mentorship.

Senior IT Coordinator will be the primary L2/L3 escalation point for complex technical issues, keeping our global IT infrastructure stable, secure and efficient. The role has three parts: advanced hands-on troubleshooting and system administration, day-to-day management of our Managed Service Provider (MSP), vendors and other service providers against agreed SLAs and using company-approved AI tools to make support faster and more self-service.

This role will involve working in rotating shifts based on business requirements to support TAG’s global IT operations and service delivery. The candidate must be flexible and willing to work across different shifts, including occasional adjustments to working hours, depending on business needs and operational priorities

All interested candidates must submit a cover letter, resume, and references via the application portal on our website. Due to the volume of applications received, responses from our recruiting team may be delayed. No phone calls or emails and whatsApp messages, please.

Responsibilities

  • Education and experience: Bachelor’s degree in IT or a related field, or equivalent experience, plus 8+ years in IT support or coordination.
  • MSP and ITSM: proven experience managing an MSP, SLAs and escalations using ITSM tools such as ServiceNow, Jira Service Management or Freshservice.
  • ITIL: working knowledge of incident, major incident, problem and escalation management, applied in a live service environment.
  • Apple and Microsoft 365: strong Apple device support and MDM experience, plus Microsoft 365 and Entra ID administration.
  • Networking: LAN/WAN, Wi-Fi, VPN, DNS, DHCP, VLANs and firewalls.
  • Servers and cloud: Windows Server or Linux, Active Directory, VMware or Hyper-V, and AWS, Azure or Google Workspace.
  • Identity: role-based access, SSO and MFA using Entra ID or Okta.
  • Backup and DR: tools such as Veeam, Acronis, Datto or native cloud backup.
  • Security: EDR (e.g. Defender, CrowdStrike), patch management, SIEM and vulnerability scanning; awareness of ISO 27001, SOC 2 or GDPR.
  • Meeting rooms and AV: hands-on experience supporting Microsoft Teams Rooms and video-conferencing equipment, and working with OEMs to resolve issues.
  • AI: practical experience using AI tools such as Microsoft Copilot to speed up diagnosis, triage and user communication in IT support.
  • Communication: excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain technical issues in plain language to users and leadership.
  • Preferred certifications: Apple and endpoint — ACSP, Jamf 100/200, Microsoft 365 Endpoint Administrator; Service management — ITIL 4 Foundation Networking — CCNA or Network+ Cloud — AWS Cloud Practitioner or AZ-104; Security — Security+ or SC-900; AI — AI-900.

We value professionals who are proactive in exploring new ways to work smarter. Ideal candidates will be comfortable using artificial intelligence tools — or excited to learn how — to increase efficiency, enhance analysis or deliverables, and generate innovative solutions. Familiarity with generative AI platforms or a growth mindset toward emerging technologies is a plus.

Candidates must be eligible to work in India and are expected to work in-person at the TAG GCE Gurugram office five days per week.

Requirements

Infrastructure, security and operations
  • Infrastructure: maintain LAN/WAN, Wi-Fi, servers and data centres, along with cloud platforms and workspaces (AWS, Azure, Microsoft 365, Google Workspace).
  • Identity and access: manage onboarding/offboarding, credentials, role-based access and MFA.
  • Lifecycle management: procure, configure, deploy and upgrade laptops, mobile devices and business applications.
  • L2/L3 escalation: be the escalation point for complex issues such as network outages, server crashes and security alerts.
  • Security and compliance: work with cybersecurity teams on patching, log monitoring and regulatory compliance.
  • Backup and DR: design, test and run backup and disaster recovery plans for business continuity.
  • Collaboration spaces: keep critical meeting rooms, Teams Rooms and collaboration spaces running through proactive maintenance, and work with OEMs and providers to resolve known issues on time.
  • Stakeholder collaboration: work with internal teams to understand how IT issues affect their work and agree priorities for critical, high-impact fixes.
Apple and Microsoft 365 support
  • Troubleshoot macOS, iOS and iPadOS devices, and manage them through an MDM platform (Jamf, Kandji or Intune) integrated with Apple Business Manager.
  • Coordinate Apple repairs, AppleCare and warranty claims.
  • Support Outlook, Teams, SharePoint and OneDrive, including users, licences, MFA and Teams Rooms.
Leveraging AI for IT support
  • Use Microsoft Copilot or other company-approved AI tools to speed up diagnosis, triage and user updates.
  • Build and maintain knowledge base articles, self-service options and AI chatbots so users can resolve common issues themselves, following responsible AI practices.
Customer experience
  • Provide friendly, clear support in plain language, including white-glove support for executives and key meetings.
  • Prioritise requests by business impact, keep users informed at each stage and confirm resolution before closing every request.
MSP management and escalations
  • Act as the primary link between users and the MSP, and ensure tickets are closed within agreed SLAs.
  • Track ticket ageing daily and escalate delays through the MSP escalation matrix and IT leadership.
  • Take charge of high-impact incidents and blocked issues, coordinating the MSP, vendors and internal teams to restore service.
  • Keep users and leadership updated, and drive root cause analysis and preventive actions.
  • Run regular MSP service reviews and report on SLA compliance, ticket trends and assets.

Benefits

TAG provides competitive benefits with regular training opportunities available to its employees.

title: Regional Growth Partner
description:
Every year, thousands of families hear about AoPS Academy and submit a consultation request to see if the program is right for their child.

What happens next determines whether they enroll or never consider us again. How do we reach them quickly? How do we walk them through our process professionally and efficiently? How do we explain what makes our academic program special and what it could mean for their child? How can campuses find more families like them in the local area? And once a family enrolls, what keeps them with us?

These are the questions a Regional Growth Partner works on with campuses in their region: testing ideas, finding what works, and spreading it. You bridge HQ strategy and campus realities so that pockets of excellence at one campus show up at all of them.

In your first year, we’d like to see campuses in your portfolio with enrollment and retention plans they own, inquiries converting to consultations and enrollments at higher rates where you worked, and admissions habits that hold up even after your attention turns to other projects.

What the Regional Growth Partner will own:

  • Portfolio health. Be a strategic partner to the Director of Growth, Regional Director, Community Marketing, and Campus Directors, and build agreement on priorities so campus-level efforts add up to regional enrollment and retention goals
  • Goals and action plans. Help each campus set ambitious enrollment and retention action plans, then help carry them out
  • Conversion and retention. Strengthen admissions conversations, follow-ups, and drop-save efforts by supporting campus teams and stepping in directly when a campus needs it
  • Pipeline practices. Review pipeline health reports and conduct enrollment conversations with campus directors to build consistency across the portfolio
  • Admissions systems. Launch new campuses, establish admissions processes, train new teams, and keep inquiry handling, consultations, and follow-ups consistent across campuses
  • Local lead gen. Work with Marketing to plan an outreach and campus event calendar that fits each campus’s enrollment needs and bandwidth
  • Data into action. Use funnel data to decide where each campus needs help next, and turn what you find into a plan the campus can act on
  • Creative growth solutions. Pilot new ideas and systems with campuses, and share what works across the region
  • Partnership. Give campus teams regular in-person support, build trust with them, and represent regional needs and opportunities to HQ

The ideal candidate has:

  • Bachelor’s degree in marketing, business, or education, or 3+ years in a related role with an emphasis on customer success and retention
  • Experience managing multiple projects and campuses (or locations or accounts) at the same time
  • Experience coaching and building relationships with people on teams you don’t manage
  • The ability to read metrics and translate them into a next step
  • The ability to coach and communicate clearly across diverse teams
  • Strong organization, with attention to detail and good time management
  • Critical thinking and creative problem solving skills
  • A track record of building trust with campus teams and coaching people toward new habits instead of handing them a checklist
  • The ability to turn data into something a campus director can act on this week
  • A habit of trying new ideas small first and saying plainly when something didn’t work

Bonus points for:

  • Experience marketing to parents and families, or working in education, enrichment, or youth programs
  • Experience launching in new markets or opening new locations
  • Familiarity with AoPS, math contests, or the kids who love them

Why Join AoPS:

This is a remote full-time position for candidates based in the Bay Area, with 10-15% travel required to campuses across the region, depending on campus needs. The hiring range for this position is $115,000 - $123,625. Here are some things you can look forward to:

  • Impact: Your work decides whether families who reach out to a campus end up enrolling, and whether they stay
  • Flexibility: Casual work environment with flexible scheduling
  • Benefits: Multiple options for Medical, Dental and Vision plans
  • Future Planning: 401(k) with company match
  • Quality of Life: PTO Plan and supportive leadership that gives you the work-life balance you deserve

Background Check:

Please note that employment is contingent on the successful completion of a background check.

Work Authorization:

Please note that in order to be considered for this position you must be legally authorized to work in the US. We are unable to offer sponsorship, including STEM-OPT and H-1B.

About AoPS:

Art of Problem Solving (AoPS) is on a mission to discover, inspire, and train the great problem solvers of the next generation. Since 2003, we have trained hundreds of thousands of the country’s top students, including nearly all the members of the US International Math Olympiad team, through our online school, in-person academies, textbooks, and online learning systems. While our primary focus has been math for most of our history, through the years we have expanded our unique problem solving curriculum into more subjects, such as language arts, science, and computer science.

title: IT Security Lead
description:
About Your Role

As our IT Security Lead at QGenda, you will serve as a senior individual contributor responsible for leading IT security operations, risk management, and governance, risk, and compliance (GRC) initiatives across our IT systems, infrastructure, and SaaS applications. You will identify and reduce risk, strengthen security controls, and mature our GRC program from policy and control design through audit readiness, evidence collection, and remediation. Working closely with IT and Help Desk, Legal, Product Development, and business teams, you will streamline control management and help ensure alignment with applicable security standards. You will also partner with Product Development’s security team to align enterprise IT security with QGenda’s broader security program.

How You’ll Make an Impact

  • Lead IT security operations and advance QGenda’s enterprise IT security strategy and GRC initiatives, translating business objectives and risk priorities into measurable improvements.
  • Oversee security controls across QGenda’s IT platforms and assets, including identity, endpoints, SaaS applications, and network infrastructure. Promote secure architecture and configuration, assess control effectiveness and attack surface, address gaps, define security metrics, and report security posture to executive leadership.
  • Serve as IT’s primary security subject matter expert (SME), providing daily guidance to IT Systems Administrators and Help Desk teams supporting IT, CRM, and Procurement on secure configuration and control implementation. Partner with system owners to drive remediation.
  • Collaborate with IT, Help Desk, and business stakeholders to align security initiatives with business objectives and integrate security into enterprise IT projects, system changes, and operational processes. Coordinate with Product Development’s security team where initiatives overlap.
  • Lead the IT vulnerability management program, including regular scans and assessments, risk-based prioritization, timely remediation and patching, and validation of fixes.
  • Lead internal and external IT security audits and compliance assessments, including control mapping, evidence coordination, gap analysis, remediation tracking, and audit readiness.
  • Improve GRC operations by automating control testing, evidence collection, and compliance workflows, and establishing ongoing monitoring of control status.
  • Develop, implement, and maintain IT security policies, standards, and best practices aligned with applicable frameworks, audit requirements, regulations, and customer and contractual obligations including NIST, ISO 27001, SOC 1, SOC 2, SOX, HIPAA, and FedRAMP, as applicable.
  • Evaluate security risks associated with internal AI adoption and other new technologies, including configuration, data exposure, vulnerabilities, and potential impacts to existing controls. Recommend appropriate safeguards.
  • Coordinate incident preparedness and response with relevant teams, capture lessons learned, and provide security awareness training and guidance to staff.

Who You Are

  • You operate effectively as a senior individual contributor, independently leading cross-functional security initiatives that measurably improve security posture and influencing teams across IT and the business.
  • You bring hands-on experience securing enterprise IT environments across identity and access management, endpoints, SaaS applications, network infrastructure, and macOS and Windows environments.
  • You have experience with enterprise security and IT platforms such as Okta, Zscaler, CrowdStrike, Google Workspace, Microsoft, Jamf, Intune, and Meraki, or comparable tools.
  • You understand enterprise risk management and GRC, and can apply frameworks and requirements such as NIST, ISO 27001, SOC 1, SOC 2, SOX, HIPAA, and FedRAMP, as applicable, to practical security controls.
  • You have experience leading or supporting security audits and compliance assessments in highly regulated environments with extensive compliance requirements, including working with auditors, mapping controls, gathering evidence, remediating gaps, and monitoring controls. You’re familiar with GRC automation and continuous monitoring platforms. Familiarity with tools such as Vanta is a plus.
  • You have experience managing vulnerability programs, including scanning, risk prioritization, remediation coordination, patching, and validation. Familiarity with tools such as Tenable is a plus.
  • You can assess security risks in SaaS applications, internal AI tools, and emerging technologies, including configuration, access, data exposure, vulnerabilities, and impacts to existing controls. You can also use AI and machine learning to improve security workflows while maintaining human oversight and critical judgment.
  • You have experience supporting incident response and security awareness. You communicate effectively with internal and external stakeholders and can explain cybersecurity principles and risks to technical and nontechnical audiences.

Experience You Bring

  • Minimum of 5 years of experience in IT security, GRC, security engineering, security operations, or related fields.
  • Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university.

title: Armed Security- Flex Patrol

Position Overview

We are seeking a reliable, professional Flex Security Officer to support safety and security operations at retail store. Logistics and Compensation

• Location: Miami, FL

• Job Type: Hours vary

• Pay Rate: $19.00 to $20.00 per hour

Availability & Schedule

• Our scheduling is based on business needs meaning shifts and hours may vary.

They communicate clearly, uphold high customer service standards, and represent the community with a polished and respectful presence in a fast paced, high-end setting.

• Monitor CCTV and alarm systems to ensure constant site awareness.

• Sound alarms or call police/fire departments immediately in the event of fire, medical emergencies, or the presence of unauthorized persons.

• Respond promptly to all incidents, emergencies, and disturbances on the property.

• Permit authorized persons to enter property by verifying guest/vendor credentials and monitoring all entrances and exits.

• Warn violators of rule infractions, such as loitering, smoking, or carrying forbidden articles, while ensuring all property rules and post orders are strictly enforced.

• Investigate and prepare detailed reports on accidents, incidents, and suspicious activities.

• Provide high-level customer service by aiding residents, members, employees, and visitors in a courteous and professional manner.

• Act as a visual deterrent to crime while maintaining a safe and secure environment for all patrons.

Licensing

• Possess valid Florida Class D and G security licenses

• Possess valid Driver’s License

Minimum Requirements

• High School Diploma or equivalent

• 21 years of age or older

• Ability to pass background screening and drug test

• Ability to pass a mental health assessment

• Reliable transportation

Skills Required

• Clear verbal and written communication skills

• Active listening skills

• Ability to assess and evaluate situations effectively

• Ability to identify critical issues quickly and accurately

• Strong customer service skills

• Ability to remain calm under pressure

• Good judgment and situational awareness

• Professional appearance, demeanor, and attitude

Preferred Qualifications

• 1 year of experience in a gated country club environment performing patrol, gatehouse, and security dispatch duties

• Experience with alarm systems and responding to alarm activations

• Experience with ABDI gate access system

• Experience with Avigilon camera systems

Other

• Must be a U.S. citizen or a foreign citizen authorized to legally work in the United States

• Must be able to successfully complete all training required for the position

Physical Requirements & Work Environment

• Indoor and outdoor assignments. Exposure to various weather conditions

• Major Activities: Extended standing, walking, and sitting. Listening, observing, communicating

• Environmental Exposure: Ability to perform duties in both indoor and outdoor settings. Must be capable of working in diverse weather conditions, including extreme heat, cold, and rain, for extended periods.

• Hazardous Conditions: Occasional exposure to high-stress situations, including responding to emergencies or physical disturbances.

• Stationary & Mobile Positions: Ability to remain in a stationary position (sitting or standing), walk for extended periods, traverse the property, or move between posts for the duration of an 8-hour shift, or as operationally required. Must be able to maintain constant alertness and professional posture throughout the assigned period.

• Patrol Requirements: Ability to continuously walk on various surfaces including pavement, grass, and uneven terrain while conducting interior and exterior rounds.

• Emergency Response: Must be able to react quickly to emergency situations, which may include running, climbing stairs, or navigating obstacles.

title: Kinship Specialist
description:
Under the general supervision of the FCS Director of Specialized Family Focused Services, the Kinship Specialist supports kinship caregivers to promote placement stability, reunification, and child safety. Referrals originate with the Iowa Department of Health and Human Services (HHS); referrals for CFI’s subcontracted kinship services are received directly from the contract holder. The position requires travel throughout the assigned service area.


Provide culturally responsive support to kinship caregivers of all races, religions, ages, genders, gender expressions, sexual orientations, socioeconomic backgrounds, and physical or mental health circumstances. Services aim to increase kinship placements, reduce placements with unrelated foster caregivers, promote placement stability, and reduce repeat maltreatment.


Key Responsibilities

Caregiver Engagement and Direct Services

  • Engage families and orient them to FCS Kinship Navigation Services within required contract timelines.
  • Independently assess caregiver strengths and needs using evidence-based tools.
  • Identify formal and informal family supports using ecomaps and other assessment tools.
  • Develop a Kinship Care Plan with caregivers that includes action steps tied to identified outcomes. Help caregivers locate affordable child care, access medical, dental, and mental health services, and meet basic needs such as clothing, beds, cribs, furniture, food, and transportation.
  • Connect caregivers with resources such as food and child care assistance, the Family Investment Program (FIP), health insurance, and legal aid. Assist with applications as needed.
  • Connect caregivers with counseling, parent education, support groups, and other supportive services.
  • Provide information about the kinship caregiver payment program and foster care licensing options.
  • Facilitate collaboration between biological parents and kinship caregivers when requested by the contract holder and/or HHS. Help caregivers understand expectations for supervising family interactions and provide training to prepare for and manage potential challenges. Communicate any limitations or concerns to the FCS Director of Specialized Family Focused Services and the Contract Supervisor.
  • Assist kinship caregivers interested in becoming licensed foster or adoptive parents with applications and required paperwork.
  • Meet all direct-service requirements established in the FCS Kinship Navigation Services contract, including meeting frequency and duration.
  • Work a schedule that responds to family and program needs, including evenings and some weekends. Provide services in the family’s home whenever possible.

Collaboration and Caregiver Support

  • Attend Child Safety Conferences, Family Focused Meetings, case reviews, unit meetings, and court hearings as requested by kinship caregivers to provide support and resource information. Attend in person unless virtual participation is permitted.
  • Maintain regular communication, as appropriate, with the FCS Director of Specialized Family Focused Services, the Contract Supervisor, and/or the HHS worker regarding caregiver participation, resource needs, and family supports. Collaborate with other service professionals and community providers.
  • Assist with developing and facilitating kinship caregiver supports, which may include in-person or virtual support groups, newsletters, and social media groups.

Documentation and Contract Compliance

  • Complete and maintain case-specific intake paperwork, assessments, notes, and reports in designated electronic systems according to contract requirements and CFI policies.
  • Complete all reporting and data collection required by the contract holder accurately and within established deadlines.
  • Complete month-end billing and expense reports within deadlines established by the contract and agency policy.
  • Protect client confidentiality in verbal, written, and electronic communications and maintain secure client records in accordance with applicable confidentiality requirements and policies.

title: Solution Architect (Chicago / Hybrid)
description:
Work. Serve. Thrive.

Imagine a place where your talent can make a meaningful difference in peoples' lives. Working at Feeding America is a uniquely rewarding experience in which our employees work together as vital parts of a much larger mission. We are innovative, mission-focused, diverse, collaborative, values-driven and focused on results.

Feeding America is the nation’s largest charity and the leading domestic hunger-relief charity in the United States. Our mission is to feed America's hungry through a nationwide network of member food banks and engage our country in the fight to end hunger.

Learn more about Feeding America here.

This position is based out of Feeding America’s Chicago office. At Feeding America, we believe in offering a flexible work environment. Employees can be in the office an average of 2-3 days a week (when not travelling for work) and work from home on other days. Employees also have access to a 30-day “work anywhere” program during the course of each calendar year that can be combined with PTO and/or holidays.

The Opportunity

The Solution Architect provides technical architecture leadership for Feeding America’s Microsoft Dynamics 365 Finance and Supply Chain Management platform and its connections to the broader technology ecosystem. The role translates business, data, security, integration and operational needs into sustainable solution designs, governs key technical decisions and guides implementation partners and internal teams. The position is accountable for architectural direction and platform design, while partnering with platform administration, cybersecurity, data and service teams that execute day-to-day operations.

Compensation

Here at Feeding America national organization, equality is central to our mission and is an integral part of our compensation policies and structures. As such, we maintain transparent salary ranges and clearly defined practices for how our team, including new hire salary offers, moves through these ranges. You can expect us to offer the best salary up front based on these clearly defined pay practices with little room for negotiation. We make exceptions for highly experienced (multiple years of at-level experience) new hires in accordance with our pay practices. Once hired, employees have the opportunity to progress through salary ranges via regular merit increases and step promotions.

Salary Range: $130,491 - $142,000 Based on Experience

Responsibilities:

  • Establishes and maintains the solution architecture and multiyear technical roadmap for Dynamics 365 Finance and Supply Chain Management in alignment with Feeding America technology strategy and enterprise architecture standards.
  • Designs end-to-end solutions that align business processes, applications, data, integrations, identity, security, infrastructure and support requirements.
  • Leads architecture reviews and documents material decisions, standards, exceptions, risks, dependencies and technical debt through established governance and Design Authority forums.
  • Defines reusable patterns and guardrails for configuration, extensibility, integrations, data movement, reporting and environment lifecycle management, emphasizing standard capabilities before customization.
  • Provides architectural oversight and direction to implementation partners, software vendors and internal delivery teams while ensuring Feeding America retains ownership of designs, roadmaps and key technical decisions.
  • Partners with platform administration and Infrastructure Services to establish environment, release, monitoring, operational-readiness, resilience and support requirements for the Dynamics 365 ecosystem.
  • Partners with Cybersecurity and business control owners to incorporate role-based access, segregation of duties, identity, auditability, privacy and regulatory controls into solution designs.
  • Guides integration and data architecture across Dynamics 365, Microsoft Power Platform, Dataverse, Azure services, enterprise data platforms and connected third-party systems.
  • Evaluates proposed enhancements and platform changes for business value, architectural fit, lifecycle cost, supportability, scalability and risk; recommends simplification and rationalization opportunities.
  • Creates and maintains current architecture artifacts and transfers knowledge to administrators, analysts, engineers, support teams and business partners to strengthen internal capability and reduce vendor dependency.

Required Experience and Qualifications:

  • 5+ years of relevant technology experience, including experience with Microsoft Dynamics 365 Finance and Supply Chain Management.
  • Demonstrated experience architecting and delivering Microsoft Dynamics 365 Finance and Supply Chain Management or comparable enterprise resource planning solutions in complex, multi-environment organizations.
  • Ability to develop solution designs spanning applications, business processes, integrations, data, identity, security, environments and operational support.
  • Working knowledge of Dynamics 365 lifecycle, extensibility and integration capabilities, including Lifecycle Services, Data Management Framework, Dataverse, application programming interfaces and Microsoft Power Platform.
  • Experience leading architecture reviews, technical decision-making and governance across internal teams and external implementation partners.
  • Experience evaluating configuration, customization and integration choices for scalability, supportability, lifecycle cost and risk.
  • Ability to communicate complex technical decisions to business, technology and executive stakeholders and produce clear architecture documentation.

Preferred Competencies, Experience and Certifications:

  • Experience with nonprofit finance, grants, procurement, inventory, warehousing or distribution operations.
  • Experience with Microsoft Azure integration services, enterprise data platforms, reporting architecture or Financial Reporting and Electronic Reporting.
  • Relevant Microsoft Dynamics 365 or Azure architecture certification
    Required Leadership Competencies:
    • Fosters an Enterprise Mindset
    • Fosters an Open and Supportive Environment
    • Leads with Accountability
    • Collaborates Internally and Externally
    • Focuses on People and Teams
    • Manages Organization and Business Complexity
    • Communicates with Impact and Influence

    Feeding America’s goal is to attract, develop, retain, and promote a talented diverse workforce where all employees feel a sense of belonging and contribute to a culture that values differences, ideas, and experiences. We intentionally seek out diverse perspectives and skills on our teams, knowing that it makes us stronger as an organization and better equipped to serve our neighbors in need. We encourage all individuals, including those from historically under-represented communities and individuals with lived experience of hunger, to apply.

    Feeding America participates in E-Verify and will provide the federal government with your Form I-9 information to confirm that you are authorized to work in the U.S. If E-Verify cannot confirm that you are authorized to work, this employer is required to give you written instructions and an opportunity to contact Department of Homeland Security (DHS) or Social Security Administration (SSA) so you can begin to resolve the issue before the employer can take any action against you, including terminating your employment. Employers can only use E-Verify once you have accepted a job offer and completed the Form I-9.

title: Manager Supplier Quality, IID/Connectivity/ASPICE
description:
Here at Scout Motors, we're carrying forward the heritage of one of the most iconic American vehicles in history. A vehicle dating back to 1960. One that forged the path for future generations of rugged SUVs and trucks and will do so once again.

But Scout is more than just a brand, it’s a legacy steeped in a culture of exploration, caretaking, and hard work.

The Scout brand is all about respect. Respect for the past and the future by taking an iconic American brand that hasn’t been around for a while, electrifying it, digitizing it, and loading it with American innovation. Respect for communities by creating a company that stands for its people and its customers. Respect for both work and play, with vehicles that are equally at home at a camp site, a job site, or on a Tuesday commute. And respect for our customers by developing two powertrains that meet their requirements — an all-electric powertrain as well as the Harvester™ range extender powertrain which includes a built-in gas-powered generator with an estimated 500 miles of combined range.

At Scout Motors, we empower our talented, inclusive, and entrepreneurial teams to innovate. What makes a Scout employee? Someone who is a visionary and a leader, who seeks new paths and shares lessons learned. A knowledgeable doer who collaborates across the company to build better. A go-getter with unrivaled passion.

Join us at Scout Motors and be part of shaping the future of transportation. If you're ready to drive change and make history, apply now!

What you’ll do

Become part of an iconic brand that is set to revolutionize the electric pick-up truck & rugged SUV marketplace by achieving the following:

  • Lead the integration of vehicles with digital networks, enabling real-time data exchange, enhanced safety, personalized experiences to support innovation, and competitive differentiation.
  • Support the development of advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS) features, traffic management, predictive maintenance and safety critical systems such as adaptive cruise control, lane-keeping assistance, and emergency braking relying on real-time data exchange.
  • Assist in the development Infotainment and personalization features, tailored media, voice assistants, and digital cockpit experience.
  • Lead the application of automotive software process standards (ASPICE) to design, implement, and improve development processes. Lead compliance activities, audits, and continuous improvement initiatives, ensuring projects meet OEM and industry quality requirements.
  • Act as the ASPICE interface with stakeholders, customers, and OEM partners; Communicate process changes, risks, and improvements to all relevant parties.
  • Lead all supplier quality planning and execution of manufacturing, assembly techniques and quality control processes from the advanced development phase to serial production.
  • Lead and oversee all quality performance and functional standards quality in all vehicle activities are met in the supply chain to ensure Customer satisfaction.
  • Ensure professional business acumen of SQEs at Suppliers to ensure Scout’s Quality expectations and core values are met and that suppliers can meet the industrialization related activities on time with the Supplier Quality team .
  • Responsible that suppliers will meet industrialization, to schedule, and at cost to ensure quality.
  • Responsible for Supplier PPAPs and ongoing activities within the Supply Chain.
  • Work as a partner with the Supply Chain to ensure escalations of issues are raised, and resolutions are solved in a timely manner.
  • Lead supplier improvements in cost, quality and manufacturability.
  • Responsible for ensuring supplier audits and corrective actions are completed on time.
  • Collaborate with Scout’s Design, Quality, and Manufacturing to determine the ideal performance specifications and supplier metrics.
  • Accountable for ongoing monitoring supplier manufacturing process development, launch readiness for new products and design changes.
  • Drive continuous improvement activities utilizing Lean Manufacturing principles.
  • Ensure suppliers have exceptionally robust processes and procedures to promote mass industrialization through efficient and seamless production of high-quality products.
  • Build a team of Supplier Quality professionals to ensure the utmost caliber of supplier audits are conducted and build partnerships within the supply chain.
  • Mentor team members, foster a culture of learning, and facilitate skill development to enhance the capabilities of the Supplier Quality team.
  • Work cross functionally with other departments within Scout
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Location & Travel Expectations:

  • This role will be based out of the Scout Motors location in Blythewood, South Carolina.
  • This role requires 5 days per week in the office, with regular in-person meetings and events.
  • Applicants should expect that the role will require the ability to convene with Scout colleagues in person and travel to participate in events on behalf of the company from time to time.
  • Travel: Domestic and international travel required, approximately 50-80% of the time. Valid driver's license required. Passport required

What you’ll bring

We expect all Scout employees to have integrity, curiosity, resourcefulness, and strive to exhibit a positive attitude, as well as a growth mindset. You’ll be comfortable with change and flexible in a fast-paced, high-growth environment. You’ll take a collaborative approach to achieve ambitious goals. Here's what else you'll bring:

  • Bachelor’s in Mechanical/Vehicle/Electrical/Industrial Engineering, Mechatronics, Business or related field; Master’s a plus.
  • 7 – 10 years of experience in automotive engineering/product quality, with at least 3 years in a leadership role with disciplinary or technical leadership responsibility in an OEM/ Tier 1.
  • Experience in Quality Systems a plus: QTR/QPNi/PPA/VDA 6.3/VDA 6.5/SAMSON/ AVON/ TEVON/LiOn/BeOn.
  • Demonstrated proven technical leadership ability with regards to sensors, cameras, radar, LiDAR, and onboard software to interpret the vehicle’s surroundings.
  • Lead cross-functional Supplier Quality task force involving Engineering, Manufacturing, Purchasing, Supplier Readiness, Production Quality, and Suppliers.
  • Sound knowledge of vehicle development, vehicle production and Supply Chain Management.
  • Financial Acumen Required.
  • In-depth knowledge of Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing (GD&T) and inspection.
  • Understanding of safety requirements.
  • Understanding of IATF, VDA, ISO, DIN, and regulatory requirements: Lead or support supplier process audits, VDA 6.3 Potential Analysis, and Supplier Risk Assessments.
  • Strong teamwork and communication skills, a high level of assertiveness as well as entrepreneurial thinking and goal- and result-oriented decision-making skills.
  • Leadership and team management abilities, with a track record of building and leading high-performing teams.
  • Proven ability to execute Program Management from a leadership level.
  • Strong technical writing ability using SPC and data analysis as well as an ability to explain complex issues in a concise and plain manner.

title: Product Manager – Automotive (Mexico Market Focus)

We are looking for a Product Manager to lead product planning and execution for the automotive portfolio in Mexico.


This role goes beyond traditional product management. We are looking for someone who can independently assess the market, challenge assumptions, and drive product and pricing decisions based on a deep understanding of the Mexican automotive landscape.


The ideal candidate is a business‑oriented product leader, not just a process executor, capable of translating market insights into clear and actionable product strategies.


Position Objective


Own the end‑to‑end product lifecycle for assigned vehicle lines in Mexico, ensuring strong competitiveness, profitability, and alignment with local customer needs.

Act as the key bridge between global strategy and local execution, adapting and challenging global inputs when necessary to fit the Mexican market reality.

  • Manage the full product lifecycle (launch, updates, pricing, positioning, phase‑out) for vehicle lines in Mexico.
  • Define market-driven product and pricing strategies, grounded in local competition, customer behavior, and commercial objectives.
  • Lead new vehicle launches and lifecycle updates, ensuring strong market positioning and dealer readiness.
  • Develop and challenge pricing structures, product mix, and value propositions, balancing volume and profitability.
  • Translate market intelligence into clear product decisions, not just analysis.
  • Work closely with HQ to align strategies while ensuring local relevance and competitiveness.
  • Drive cross‑functional coordination across Marketing, Sales, Aftersales, Finance, Supply Chain, and Engineering.
  • Monitor and interpret competitive landscape, pricing evolution, and market trends in Mexico.
  • Build business cases based on first-principles thinking, not only existing tools or frameworks.


Required Experience


  • 10+ years of experience in automotive product roles (OEM).
  • Proven experience managing vehicle lines or product portfolios specifically for the Mexican market.
  • Direct involvement in: Product lifecycle management, vehicle launches and pricing and positioning decisions
  • Experience working with global/HQ teams, with the ability to localize strategy.
  • Strong exposure to competitive analysis and market intelligence in Mexico.


Critical Requirements (Must-Have)


  • Deep understanding of the Mexican automotive market and competitive dynamics.
  • Demonstrated ability to make independent product and pricing decisions.
  • Ability to clearly explain the business logic behind decisions (not just processes).
  • Evidence of challenging or adapting global strategies to local realities.
  • Hands-on mindset with strong ownership of deliverables and outcomes.


Technical Skills


  • Product Lifecycle Management (PLM)
  • Pricing strategy and financial analysis
  • Market intelligence and competitive benchmarking
  • Forecasting and business case development


Core Competencies


  • Strong critical thinking and problem-solving
  • Ability to question assumptions and think independently
  • High level of ownership and accountability
  • Clear and structured communication
  • Ability to operate in ambiguous, fast-changing environments


What We Are NOT Looking For


  • Profiles limited to regional/global coordination without local ownership
  • Candidates who rely only on established tools and frameworks without understanding their logic
  • Purely operational or execution-only profiles

title: Kinship Specialist
description:
Under the general supervision of the FCS Director of Specialized Family Focused Services, the Kinship Specialist supports kinship caregivers to promote placement stability, reunification, and child safety. Referrals originate with the Iowa Department of Health and Human Services (HHS); referrals for CFI’s subcontracted kinship services are received directly from the contract holder. The position requires travel throughout the assigned service area.


Provide culturally responsive support to kinship caregivers of all races, religions, ages, genders, gender expressions, sexual orientations, socioeconomic backgrounds, and physical or mental health circumstances. Services aim to increase kinship placements, reduce placements with unrelated foster caregivers, promote placement stability, and reduce repeat maltreatment.


Key Responsibilities

Caregiver Engagement and Direct Services

  • Engage families and orient them to FCS Kinship Navigation Services within required contract timelines.
  • Independently assess caregiver strengths and needs using evidence-based tools.
  • Identify formal and informal family supports using ecomaps and other assessment tools.
  • Develop a Kinship Care Plan with caregivers that includes action steps tied to identified outcomes. Help caregivers locate affordable child care, access medical, dental, and mental health services, and meet basic needs such as clothing, beds, cribs, furniture, food, and transportation.
  • Connect caregivers with resources such as food and child care assistance, the Family Investment Program (FIP), health insurance, and legal aid. Assist with applications as needed.
  • Connect caregivers with counseling, parent education, support groups, and other supportive services.
  • Provide information about the kinship caregiver payment program and foster care licensing options.
  • Facilitate collaboration between biological parents and kinship caregivers when requested by the contract holder and/or HHS. Help caregivers understand expectations for supervising family interactions and provide training to prepare for and manage potential challenges. Communicate any limitations or concerns to the FCS Director of Specialized Family Focused Services and the Contract Supervisor.
  • Assist kinship caregivers interested in becoming licensed foster or adoptive parents with applications and required paperwork.
  • Meet all direct-service requirements established in the FCS Kinship Navigation Services contract, including meeting frequency and duration.
  • Work a schedule that responds to family and program needs, including evenings and some weekends. Provide services in the family’s home whenever possible.

Collaboration and Caregiver Support

  • Attend Child Safety Conferences, Family Focused Meetings, case reviews, unit meetings, and court hearings as requested by kinship caregivers to provide support and resource information. Attend in person unless virtual participation is permitted.
  • Maintain regular communication, as appropriate, with the FCS Director of Specialized Family Focused Services, the Contract Supervisor, and/or the HHS worker regarding caregiver participation, resource needs, and family supports. Collaborate with other service professionals and community providers.
  • Assist with developing and facilitating kinship caregiver supports, which may include in-person or virtual support groups, newsletters, and social media groups.

Documentation and Contract Compliance

  • Complete and maintain case-specific intake paperwork, assessments, notes, and reports in designated electronic systems according to contract requirements and CFI policies.
  • Complete all reporting and data collection required by the contract holder accurately and within established deadlines.
  • Complete month-end billing and expense reports within deadlines established by the contract and agency policy.
  • Protect client confidentiality in verbal, written, and electronic communications and maintain secure client records in accordance with applicable confidentiality requirements and policies.

title: Manager, Global Sports Asset Strategy
description:
About Us

Fanatics is a leading global sports platform redefining how fans connect with the teams, players and moments they love. Our businesses — Fanatics Commerce, Fanatics Collectibles, Fanatics Betting & Gaming, Fanatics Events, Fanatics Advertising, Fanatics Markets and Fanatics Studios — maximize the presence and reach for hundreds of partners globally and create a one-stop experience that allows fans to buy, bet, collect, and earn, while engaging with sports in deeper, more immersive ways. This includes licensed fan gear and lifestyle products, sportsbook and iGaming, physical and digital trading cards, live events, premium sports entertainment content, credit card offerings and more. Together, they form a powerful, integrated ecosystem — connected by the Fanatics ONE loyalty program and FanCash, the currency of sport — delivering personalized experiences to over 100 million fans worldwide. Fanatics holds partnerships with over 900 sports properties, from professional leagues and players’ associations to teams, colleges and retail partners; over 7,000 athletes and celebrities; and over 2,000 retail locations, including all Lids stores. Backed by a team of more than 22,000 employees, Fanatics is committed to relentlessly enhancing the fan experience.

About the Company

Fanatics Collectibles is a new company operating at the intersection of collectibles, culture, and technology. Backed by world-class investors, operators, and sports & entertainment partners, we are building the global leader in next-generation collectibles. As part of the broader Fanatics ecosystem, we leverage a digital sports platform that spans over 900 sports properties and engages more than 81 million fans. Together, we are reimagining every part of the collectibles experience for fans, partners, and creators.

Role Summary

The Asset Manager will help build and execute the strategy, planning and management of relics and autographs used across Fanatics Collectibles’ global football products. Reporting into the Director of Football Product Development, this person will work closely with Product Development, Product Strategy, Athlete Partnerships, Licensing, and Relic/Auto Operations and other teams to determine how assets are planned for, allocated and deployed across products and markets.

The role requires strong inventory and data management skills, commercial judgment and deep knowledge of global football, including leagues, clubs, players and associations.

Responsibilities:

  • Develop and manage the global asset and relic strategy for football products.
  • Partner with Product Development to understand product plans and determine asset requirements across releases, brands and markets.
  • Act as the central liaison between Product Management, Athlete Partnerships, Licensing and Operations.
  • Create allocation plans that determine how assets and relics are deployed across products, especially across key and high value/finite inventory
  • Maintain a clear view of available inventory, future requirements and gaps.
  • Manage different asset and inventory types, including player-worn, match-used, event-used and other authenticated materials.
  • Balance the use of high-value assets across premium, core and entry-level products.
  • Use product forecasts, player relevance, market demand and inventory levels to guide deployment decisions.
  • Identify opportunities to maximize the value and lifespan of available assets.
  • Support the acquisition of new assets through clubs, leagues, associations, athletes and other partners.
  • Monitor inventory health and identify shortages, excess inventory, duplication and upcoming requirements.
  • Build reporting and dashboards to support product planning and decision-making.
  • Ensure asset usage complies with licensing agreements, contractual rights and partner requirements.
  • Support annual and seasonal planning across global football products, including helping to establish and manage portfolio wide budgets.
  • Help improve asset-management systems, data quality and working processes as the business grows.
  • May support F1 auto and relic asset management and strategy as needed.

Experience and Skills Required:

  • 5–7 years of experience in asset management, inventory strategy, product planning, supply chain, licensing operations or a related field.
  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent professional experience.
  • Strong knowledge of global football, including major leagues, clubs, players, national teams and governing associations.
  • Experience managing physical inventory, product components or other high-value assets.
  • Strong analytical skills and confidence working with large and detailed data sets.
  • Ability to translate product plans and commercial priorities into an inventory and allocation strategy.
  • Highly organized, with strong attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple product timelines.
  • Strong cross-functional communication and stakeholder-management skills.
  • Comfortable working across global teams, markets and time zones.
  • Sound judgment when balancing asset value, product needs, contractual requirements and future opportunities.
  • Experience with inventory-management, ERP, product lifecycle or reporting systems is preferred.
  • Experience in collectibles, sports, consumer products, licensing or entertainment is an advantage.

title: FCS Unit Lead
description:
Under the general supervision of the FCS Unit Supervisor, the FCS Unit Lead supports daily operations, improves workflows, and helps monitor contract compliance. The Unit Lead audits case files for timely, thorough documentation that meets HHS standards and helps staff complete reports as needed.


The Unit Lead mentors peers, helps train new staff, and answers procedural questions. In coordination with the Unit Supervisor, the Lead helps balance workloads, assign cases promptly within designated HHS alignment teams, and communicate case coverage to HHS.


The Unit Lead serves as the first point of contact for newly referred clients, ensures required paperwork for the first 30 days is completed, and transitions cases to unit staff as staffing allows.


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Lead Responsibilities and Staff Support

  • Mentor new and existing Family Specialists and support staff through onboarding, shadowing, coaching, and modeling effective family engagement, assessment, documentation, and professional boundaries.
  • Assign and coordinate job duties, casework, family interactions, and coverage under the Unit Supervisor’s direction, considering staff qualifications, availability, workload, family needs, and contract requirements.
  • Communicate priorities, timelines, and expectations; monitor assignment completion and workload; identify service gaps; and coordinate adjustments with the supervisor.
  • Provide consultation on case planning, family engagement, community resources, and problem solving. Review documentation for completeness and timeliness and communicate training or quality concerns to the supervisor.
  • Serve as a point of contact when the supervisor is unavailable, coordinate urgent coverage and on-call responses within delegated authority, and promptly escalate safety, staffing, or service concerns. Refer formal personnel decisions to the supervisor.

Family Engagement and Direct Services

  • Gather referral information, make timely initial contacts, orient families to services, and begin engagement and assessment. Facilitate prompt family interactions following removal and support continuity until ongoing services are established.
  • Assess family strengths, needs, and formal and informal supports using evidence-based tools. Continually assess child vulnerability, threats of maltreatment, and parental protective capacity.
  • Develop case goals and service plans with families; provide counseling and skill development within the role’s scope; and make service recommendations to Iowa HHS regarding child safety and placement.
  • Arrange and provide supervised family interactions, home visits, safety services, and case coverage. Meet contract requirements for service frequency, duration, and timelines.
  • Connect families with community resources, transportation, and other supports; assist with maintaining healthy home environments; and provide client transportation as needed.
  • Provide crisis intervention, respond effectively to emergencies, and communicate safety concerns through established agency and referral-source procedures.

Coordination Documentation and Compliance

  • Coordinate schedules and services with Family Specialists, Intervention Specialists, Support Workers, referral sources, community providers, and family supports. Respond promptly and professionally to calls and emails.
  • Attend Child Safety Conferences, PRCs, Family Focuses Meetings, case reviews, unit meetings, and court hearings as requested, primarily in person unless electronic attendance is permitted. Travel to family interactions, court, medical appointments, and other service locations.
  • Complete intake paperwork, assessments, service plans, contact notes, reports, quality assurance records, billing, and month-end expense reports accurately and on time in designated systems.
  • Protect confidentiality in verbal, written, and electronic communication and maintain secure records. Follow agency policies, contract requirements, and applicable licensing and accreditation standards.
  • Work a flexible schedule based on family and program needs, including evenings, some weekends, and assigned on-call duties.
  • Proficiency with agency software, electronic documentation, and other technology required for service delivery.
